concept.name: Bulkhead & Fault Isolation
concept.tagline: Partition thread pools, connections, and queues so one slow dependency cannot exhaust all capacity.

spark.summary: The bulkhead pattern limits resources per dependency or tenant—like ship compartments—so failures stay localized.
spark.keyTakeaway: Give each risky dependency its own budget; shared pools convert partial outages into total outages.

concept.whyItMatters: Without bulkheads, one flaky partner API can stall every checkout thread.
whenNotToUse: When total pool size is smaller than minimum per-bulkhead floor

examples.title: Recommendations sidebar
examples.scenario: Slow ML service must not block payment authorization threads.
examples.outcome: Dedicated small pool for recommendations; checkout pool stays responsive.

tradeOffs.con: Under-utilization if pools are too conservative

failureModes.name: Pool exhaustion in one bulkhead
failureModes.description: Legitimate traffic rejected while other pools idle.
failureModes.mitigation: Dynamic borrowing with caps and metrics.

commonMistakes: One giant thread pool for all outbound HTTP

deepDive.markdownContent:
## Bulkheads

Isolate capacity: threads, connections, semaphores, or queues.

caseStudy.problem: Partner API slowdown froze all workers
caseStudy.impact: Checkout stayed available during partner incident

relationships.description: Bulkheads limit damage; breakers stop calling failing deps.
